description: Thirty read-back items for T5. Variant A is the value as plain words; variant B adds the only two delivery controls Coda supports — spell() for characters and [brackets] for inlineSpeedAlpha to slow a number. Items are chosen for the four ways a spoken clinical value is misheard: look-alike drug names (ISMP confused-drug list), doses whose digits carry the risk, alphanumeric codes with no redundancy, and names outside the recogniser's usual distribution. All patient data is synthetic.

variants.A: the sentence as plain words — what a listener would report hearing
variants.B: the same sentence with Rime's delivery controls: spell() and [brackets] for inlineSpeedAlpha

kinds.dose: number and unit; B must bracket the number and repeat it with spell()
kinds.lasa_dose: dose whose drug name is on the ISMP look-alike list; B must also spell the drug
kinds.pair: paired reading; B must say 'over', never 'slash', and bracket both halves
kinds.number: critical number; B must bracket it and repeat it with spell()
kinds.noted: non-critical number; it is noted rather than read back, so B must stay plain
kinds.code: alphanumeric identifier; B must be spell() of the whole code
kinds.name: person's name; B must add no markup — spelling a name is worse, not better
kinds.time: clock time; B must add no markup
